Dear Dr. Bennett,

Thank you for evaluating Mr. Arthur Vance, a 77-year-old gentleman who presents for assessment of slowly progressive weakness that first became noticeable around age 45. He is a retired accountant who manages mild hypertension with lisinopril. 

On physical examination, there is prominent bilateral wasting across the thenar eminences, accompanied by clear paresis of the intrinsic hand musculature and reduced strength in the finger flexors. Lower extremity examination demonstrates bilateral high-arched feet and an unmistakably bulky, hypertrophic appearance of the calves. Mechanical tapping of the vastus lateralis elicited rapid, rolling waves of contraction traveling across the muscle belly. Cranial nerves were completely intact, light touch and pinprick sensation were preserved, and deep tendon reflexes were normal and symmetric.

Review of systems is largely non-contributory. Mr. Vance denies any fatigue, myalgias, or muscle stiffness. He remains free of muscle spasms, and there were no tremors or other involuntary movements observed during the visit. He reports no exercise intolerance, and formal bedside cognitive testing demonstrated sharp recall and executive function with no signs of mental deterioration. 

Laboratory workup revealed an elevated circulating creatine kinase activity alongside an increased serum aspartate aminotransferase concentration. Serum lactate was entirely within the reference range, with no evidence of lactic acidosis.

I would greatly appreciate your specialized assessment and advice regarding further diagnostic evaluation.

Sincerely,
Dr. Clara Adams
